turns.t: G'day. Both my wrists are swollen and sore, and I can't say I've got much of an idea why.
Thanks for coming. When did the swelling begin?
Hard to say, mate. A while back. Couldn't tell you if it was the footy season or after.
What's it like day to day? ~
Sore in the morning, a bit better by lunch. I can still work. ~
Has anything made it better or worse? ~
Hot showers help. Typing on the laptop makes it worse. ~
Tell me about your general health. Anything long-term?
Psoriasis, on my elbows. Had it since I was a teenager.
Interesting. That matters here. Does it flare when the joints are bad? ~
Hard to say. Maybe a bit. ~
Let me explain what I think is going on. Joints are lined with a thin membrane. When it gets inflamed, it swells and hurts, and it's often worse in the morning. ~
Right. And that's what I've got? ~
It's what the pattern suggests, particularly with your psoriasis. I think this could be an inflammatory arthritis.
Arthritis. At my age. ~
It can happen at any age, and it responds well to treatment. ~
What do I do in the meantime? ~
Wear a wrist splint at night, to rest the joints. You can buy one from the pharmacy.
Will that help? ~
It usually does. Also take regular breaks from typing, and stretch your wrists every hour.
I can do that. ~
Heat, like your hot showers, is a good idea. Keep doing that. ~
Good. ~
Is there anything you're worried about? ~
Just whether I'll still be able to work. ~
Most people carry on working, with some adjustments. ~
That's a relief. ~
Let me repeat the plan. Splints at night, breaks from typing, heat in the morning. ~
Got it. ~
If the swelling isn't gone in two weeks, come back and see me.
Two weeks. Righto. ~
Good. Take care. ~
Thanks, doctor. ~
